summary: The proposal is well-structured overall, with clear problem motivation, a complete bibliography, and no issues in figures or core structure. However, three major issues need addressing: the AI transparency statement fails to name specific sections where tools were used, a key schedule deliverable is vague and non-measurable, and a prohibited 'Documentation' task appears in the schedule. Additionally, several minor issues around terminology consistency, abbreviation definitions, and measurable evaluation criteria should be tightened before submission.

findings.title: AI transparency statement does not name the specific sections where tools were used
findings.description: The AI transparency statement does not specify which sections of the proposal the AI tools were used for. It only says tools were used 'across different stages of the writing process' but never names specific sections (e.g., Abstract, Introduction, Problem, Motivation, Objective, Schedule, Bibliography). The guidelines explicitly require the statement to name 'the sections involved.' For example, the student should indicate in which sections Grammarly was applied, in which sections ChatGPT was used for content expansion, etc.

locations.section: Transparency in the Use of AI Tools
locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across **diferent stages of the writing process**.

findings.title: Vague deliverable: 'Implement core feedback generation pipeline'
findings.description: The item 'Implement core feedback generation pipeline' in Iteration 2 does not specify what the pipeline does, what its inputs/outputs are, or what a completed deliverable looks like. It reads like a generic 'implement features' task. The student should describe the concrete, measurable outcome (e.g., 'a working service that takes a thesis PDF and a guideline set as input and returns structured feedback items in JSON format, testable via API endpoint').

findings.title: Prohibited task: 'Documentation' in Iteration 9
findings.description: Rule 5 explicitly states that the schedule should not include thesis writing, documentation writing, or presentation preparation tasks. 'Documentation' as a standalone work item in Iteration 9 violates this rule. The student should remove this item; if any technical specification or API documentation is needed as part of a feature, it should be embedded within the relevant development iteration rather than listed as a separate task.

locations.quote: •   Review the system and check for bugs •   **Documentation**

findings.title: Evaluation tasks lack measurable criteria
findings.description: Iterations 5 and 6 each contain an 'Evaluate …' item ('Evaluate agentic and prompt chaining setups' and 'Evaluate different LLM models and providers') without specifying what the measurable output is. A benchmark report? Specific accuracy/latency metrics on a defined corpus? The student should state the concrete deliverable and the evaluation criteria so the iteration has a verifiable completion condition.

findings.title: Vague work item: 'Review the system and check for bugs'
findings.description: The item 'Review the system and check for bugs' in Iteration 9 is not measurable. It does not specify what is being reviewed, what criteria define a bug, or what the deliverable is. This also resembles a waterfall-style 'testing phase' at the end of the project rather than an agile increment. The student should replace this with a specific, measurable task (e.g., 'End-to-end integration test covering all four objectives passes with zero critical defects') or fold regression testing into each iteration's scope.

locations.quote: **Review the system and check for bugs**

findings.title: Inconsistent terminology for non-cloud LLM hosting: "local" vs "locally self-hosted" vs "self-hosted"
findings.description: The concept of running LLMs on university infrastructure is referred to as "local" in the Abstract, "locally self-hosted" and "self-hosted" in Section 4.3. Use one consistent term (e.g., "self-hosted") throughout the author's prose.

locations.quote: assess trade-offs between **local** and cloud hosting
careful consideration of when to use **locally self-hosted** LLMs versus cloud-hosted ones. **Self-hosted** models keep student drafts inside the university's infrastructure

findings.title: Abbreviation 'AI' used without prior definition
findings.description: The abbreviation 'AI' appears in the AI Transparency Statement (section heading and body text) but is never spelled out as 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)' earlier in the document. Per the guidelines, abbreviations should be defined before first use. Either spell it out in the section heading/body or add a brief definition on first occurrence.

locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several **AI**-based tools across different stages of the writing process.

findings.title: Paragraph too short (1 line)
findings.description: The paragraph consisting of only the sentence about the student handing in the thesis is a single line long, well below the 5-8 line guideline. It should be merged into the preceding paragraph about the iterative proposal workflow, as it provides a direct contrast to that same idea.

locations.quote: The student, by contrast, hands in the thesis itself as a single final submission.
